Created the skill. This question was answered CORRECTLY, but it surfaced a generalizable pattern not previously captured:

What was learned and saved (skill: officeqa-profile-economy-chart-quarterly-change):
- A new chart family — the "Profile of the Economy" section charts (payroll employment, unemployment, GDP, CPI) found near the FRONT of modern 2000s bulletins.
- The two-stage averaging convention for "mean of the average monthly change from end of Q1 to end of Q2": stage 1 = (June − March) / 3 months per year; stage 2 = mean of those per-year values across the inclusive year range.
- The divisor pitfall: end-Q1→end-Q2 spans 3 months (divide by 3, not by quarters or years), and the inclusive-range / thousands-units conventions.
- Verified anchor: Sep 2007 payroll employment, 2004–2006 = 202.333.

No memory update needed — this is procedural and fits cleanly in the skill. Reflection complete.
